title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Revisited: Weighted Sharpness as a Regularization Term

problem.claim: Improving DNN generalization is associated with seeking flatter minima, motivating sharpness-aware optimization.

gap.claim: The loss used by SAM is revisited to develop a more general sharpness-regularization method.

contributions.claim: WSAM incorporates sharpness as a regularization term in a more general method related to SAM.
The paper provides a generalization bound for WSAM using PAC and Bayes-PAC techniques.
WSAM is reported to improve generalization or remain highly competitive against a vanilla optimizer, SAM, and its variants.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report proving a generalization bound through combined PAC and Bayes-PAC techniques.
The authors report evaluating WSAM on various public datasets.
The authors report improved or highly competitive generalization relative to a vanilla optimizer, SAM, and its variants.

narrative_sequence.summary: DNN generalization is linked to the flatness of minima, motivating SAM.
The paper revisits SAM's loss and proposes WSAM with sharpness as a regularization term.
The paper presents a PAC and Bayes-PAC generalization bound and evaluates WSAM on public datasets.
WSAM is reported to improve or remain highly competitive in generalization against specified optimizers.
The authors provide a code link.

source_observation.claim: The method adds sharpness as a regularization term while revisiting the SAM loss.

interpretation.claim: An optimizer's generalization behavior may be addressed by making a relevant property an explicit regularization component.

application.claim: When adapting sharpness-aware optimization, consider explicit regularization formulations and evaluate them against the original optimizer and close variants.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which settings, datasets, or models benefit most from this formulation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact WSAM objective or weighting mechanism.
The abstract does not provide the generalization-bound statement or assumptions.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, models, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results or code usability.
